title: I died as a mineral
hook: Rumi: I died as mineral and became plant, died as plant and became animal (Masnavi 3.3901ff)
carry: what did I lose by dying
tomorrow: a famous 'Rumi' line: neither Christian, Jew nor Muslim. is it his?

segments.voice: Six days, six lines: before the silver cord. Each asks its own. Separate shelves. My companion text. Thank the hosts. And yesterday, the divan, signed with a friend's name. Now one more Rumi poem, this one about dying.
screen: `BEFORE THE SILVER CORD · EACH ASKS ITS OWN · SEPARATE SHELVES` → `MY COMPANION TEXT · THANK THE HOSTS · THE DIVAN`

segments.voice: Old school photos are strange: the braces, the haircut, a person you used to be and aren't anymore. Did that kid die, or grow? Rumi asks that about the whole of a life. In his long poem, the Masnavi, he tells his own story from the bottom up. I died as a mineral, he says, and became a plant. I died as a plant and rose to animal. I died as an animal, and I was human.
screen: `A PERSON YOU USED TO BE.` → `MINERAL, PLANT, ANIMAL, HUMAN.`

segments.voice: Then comes the question that's today's line: why should I fear? When was I ever less by dying? And he doesn't stop at human. Once more, he says, I will die as a man to rise among the angels, and pass beyond even the angel, into what no mind has pictured. The passage closes on the Quran's words for a time of loss: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." Here's the teaching, in Rumi's own Muslim, Sufi world. Each death on the ladder is a step on the road back to God, and every loss along the way has turned out to be a gain. Sufi readers take it as the soul's long journey home, not as a claim that you were once a rock. For anyone listening with children: this poem is about death, and it is full of hope. Worth repeating: Rumi ends his ladder of deaths with the Quran's line about returning to God.
screen: `WHEN WAS I LESS BY DYING?` · `BEYOND EVEN THE ANGEL.` · `UNTO HIM WE ARE RETURNING.` · then, large: `WHAT DID I LOSE BY DYING?`

segments.voice: Find an old photo of yourself, on your phone or in a drawer, and look at it for a while. Name one thing that person had to lose for you to grow: a fear, a habit, a certainty. Then ask Rumi's question quietly: was I less for losing it?
I died as a mineral: Rumi's ladder of deaths, each one a step up, and back toward God.
screen: `I DIED AS A MINERAL — today's word`.

segments.voice: Hold this one: what did I lose by dying, Rumi's question that answers itself. Talk soon.

chat.meaning: In the Masnavi, Rumi dies as mineral, plant and animal and rises each time. In his Sufi Islam, each death is a step back toward God.
